_note: Vermont up-front rental-charge rules under 9 V.S.A. § 4456a (Residential rental application), retrieved verbatim from legislature.vermont.gov on 2026-06-20 (amended 2025, No. 69, § 10, eff. July 1, 2025). § 4456a(a): a landlord may NOT charge any application fee to apply for a residential dwelling unit. § 4456a(b)(2): a landlord may not require a Social Security number to complete a residential rental application or refuse an application for lack of one. NOTE: Vermont's residential rental statute (Chapter 137) sets NO statutory cap or limit on late fees — § 4455 (payment of rent) is silent on late charges — so this file does NOT flag late fees; a separate Vermont primary source would be required before doing so. All rules status=draft-unverified: review by a Vermont tenant attorney / legal-aid clinic before public conclusions.

rules.title: Application / screening fee to apply for a residential unit
rules.description: Per 9 V.S.A. § 4456a(a), a landlord or a landlord's agent may not charge any application fee to apply to enter into a rental agreement for a residential dwelling unit. A lease or application that demands an 'application fee', 'screening fee', or 'processing fee' to apply for a residential rental is unenforceable as to that charge.
rules.tenant_explainer: In Vermont a landlord can't charge you anything just to apply for an apartment — application, screening, and processing fees for a residential rental are not allowed.

citations.label: 9 V.S.A. § 4456a(a)
citations.quote: A landlord or a landlord’s agent shall not charge an application fee to any individual in order to apply to enter into a rental agreement for a residential dwelling unit. This subsection shall not be construed to prohibit a person from charging a fee to a person in order to apply to rent commercial or nonresidential property.

rules.title: Social Security number required to apply
rules.description: Per 9 V.S.A. § 4456a(b)(2), a landlord or a landlord's agent may not require a Social Security number to complete a residential rental application or refuse an application because the applicant lacks one; the landlord must accept any unexpired government-issued ID, an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number, or a Social Security number (§ 4456a(b)(1)). A clause demanding a Social Security number as a condition of applying or renting is unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: A Vermont landlord can't make you give a Social Security number to apply, and can't turn you down for not having one. A government ID or an ITIN has to be accepted instead.

citations.label: 9 V.S.A. § 4456a(b)
citations.quote: (1) In order to conduct a background or credit check, a landlord shall accept any of the following: (A) an original or a copy of any unexpired form of government-issued identification; (B) an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number; or (C) a Social Security number. (2) A landlord or a landlord’s agent shall not require a Social Security number for the completion of a residential rental application or refuse to accept an application due to the lack of a Social Security number.
